threats.control: Verify the existing Ed25519 AXIOM capability format against the trusted Hypervisor key, exact issuer, exact Grid audience, and bounded lifetime.
threats.residual: A compromised Hypervisor signing key can still mint syntactically valid admission capabilities.

threats.control: Require capability subject to equal the exact Grid append actor and derive the admission JTI from actor plus exact event invocation digest.
threats.residual: This authenticates the admitted principal identifier; it does not prove human identity, legal identity, or Circle membership role.

threats.control: Bind invocation digest and exact non-extensible constraints to Circle id, deterministic event id, binding digest, expected prior Circle head, resulting head, payload digest, and persistence-policy digest.
threats.residual: Correct binding does not prove the historical record is true or legitimately governed.

threats.control: Reject unsupported event fields, capability claim fields, and constraint fields; all authority flags remain false.
threats.residual: Future schema versions require a fresh review before adding any field that could be interpreted as authority.

threats.control: Bind each token to one exact event; persist only the capability digest through the signed Grid trace id; same-token exact replay is idempotent and cannot advance the Circle head.
threats.residual: The raw capability remains a bearer credential during its short lifetime and must be protected from disclosure.

threats.control: Require the persisted signed Grid trace id to equal the digest-derived trace id of the presented token; a different token for an already-persisted deterministic event is rejected.
threats.residual: The trace proves which token digest was admitted, not why Hypervisor policy chose to issue it.

threats.control: Require the persisted Grid event actor and capability-derived trace id to match the current admitted subject on replay.
threats.residual: Circle record types still need explicit semantic rules for which Circle role or collective process may request persistence.

threats.control: Do not infer Circle decision authorship, voting authority, or collective finality from the principal that submits the decision record to Grid; Circle decisions have collective participant receipts and no single decider field.
threats.residual: A future decision-admission rule must define an explicit collective submitter or aggregation proof without converting transport identity into governance authority.

threats.control: Do not emit a separate capability-consumption event for Circle admission; the deterministic Circle persistence event itself carries the durable capability fingerprint in its signed trace id.
threats.residual: This admission model is specific to an exact deterministic Circle event and must not be generalized to arbitrary capability use.

threats.control: Reuse capability nbf/exp and bounded-TTL verification, with a 300-second absolute ceiling and a narrower local TTL limit supplied by integration.
threats.residual: The current internal helper exposes a deterministic verification-time seam for testing; runtime wiring must use the trusted service clock and configured TTL without caller override.

threats.control: Require intent, plan, and policy digests in the signed capability and bind the exact invocation digest.
threats.residual: Digest presence alone does not prove the referenced intent, plan, or policy was valid; runtime issuance must derive them from authenticated Hypervisor state.

threats.control: Policy, constraints, receipt, and outputs explicitly deny Circle-role proof, decision authority, runtime authority, portable authority, and external-effect authority.
threats.residual: Consumers must preserve the distinction between permission to persist an inert record and authority to make or execute a Circle decision.

threats.control: Grid signs an admission receipt bound to capability digest, claims digest, actor, event, Grid sequence/hash, and admission trace; receipt verification additionally requires Grid chain verification covering the event.
threats.residual: A receipt does not independently prove complete history, governance legitimacy, or distributed consensus.

threats.control: Persist only SHA-256 capability fingerprint through the signed Grid trace; never place the raw capability in Circle event payload or admission receipt.
threats.residual: Operators must still prevent raw capability leakage through logs, crash dumps, telemetry, or caller storage.

threats.control: No public or service route is wired in this slice; admission is an internal candidate around CircleGridStore.
threats.residual: CircleGridStore itself remains callable by internal code; runtime promotion must make the authenticated admission wrapper the sole service-level Circle append path.

promotion_blockers: Hypervisor issuance must originate from authenticated intent, plan, deny-dominant policy, and principal state rather than a standalone helper call.
Record-type authorization rules must define who may request invitation, membership, proposal, and collective decision persistence without inventing a false single decision actor.
The authenticated admission wrapper must become the sole service-level Circle append path; direct CircleGridStore append must remain unreachable from service routes.
The internal request must also be bound to authenticated Hypervisor service transport identity and production mTLS rather than capability possession alone.
Runtime verification must use the Grid service clock and configured capability TTL with no caller-controlled verification-time override.
Hypervisor intent, plan, and policy digests must be recoverable as authenticated evidence rather than opaque digest claims.
Issuer-key rotation, compromise response, and short-lived capability invalidation semantics require an operational runbook.
Raw capabilities must be excluded from logs, telemetry, backups, exports, and diagnostic error bodies.
Admission receipts need a supported read/verification path only if it can preserve chain-verification and privacy boundaries.
Security, privacy, governance, and accessibility review must pass before any real Circle member can invoke the path.
